newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Standard cuts prime to 19.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Standard cuts prime to 19.25 pct.

text.p: South Africa's Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it was cutting its prime lending rate to 19.25 percent from 19.50 percent, effective October 1.
Other banks showed no immediate signs of following suit, holding prime at 19.50 percent.

South African prime rates were lasted reduced on June 25, when Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd took its competitors by surprise, announcing a one percentage point cut to 19.50, effective July 1.
That move followed widespread criticism of commercial banks for unilaterally hiking rates by one point to 20.50 percent on May 17 without any lead from the central Reserve Bank.
The Reserve Bank's key has been unchanged since end-April, when it was hiked from 15 to 16 percent.
